Team,

Thanks Vanessa. I've reviewed the redline and flagged three items for discussion with BrightRetail:

1) Subprocessor notice window: our standard is 10 business days (automated list + monthly cadence). BrightRetail requested 30 days; we can offer 15 business days as a compromise.

2) Transfer Impact Language: I propose the following concise paragraph to include in the DPA (short, contract-friendly):

"Transfer Safeguards: Redwood Inference has implemented organizational and technical measures designed to provide appropriate safeguards for transfers from the EEA and UK to jurisdictions outside the EEA/UK. These include (i) execution of EU Standard Contractual Clauses (as amended); (ii) encryption of customer data in transit and at rest; (iii) strict access controls and logging for production environments; and (iv) a documented subprocessors policy with notice and objection rights. Redwood will cooperate with reasonable requests to provide evidence of measures where allowed by law and without disclosure of confidential operational details."

3) Data subject scope: ensure the DPA language maps to BrightRetail's role as controller and Redwood as processor — their proposed redline attempted to expand obligations. We should push to keep standard controller/processor allocations.

If Grant & Co have specific alternate wording for the TIA, please share; otherwise we can propose the paragraph above and include the SCCs + UK IDTA addendum as attachments. I'm fine with DocuSign execution as long as the envelope includes the redline (v3) and a short summary of negotiated items.

Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik, Vanessa — that TIA paragraph looks reasonable and concise. A couple of follow-ups from our counsel (Grant & Co):

- They asked if Redwood can commit to a 15-business-day subprocessor notice window (sounds acceptable per your note).
- For explanatory purposes, they'd like a 1-paragraph supplement to the SCCs (non-technical) that confirms Redwood's use of encryption and the fact that we will not transfer unencrypted identifiers to third parties except as described in the DPA.

Grant & Co also proposed a small edit to the controller/processor clause to more clearly state data export responsibilities during cross-border law enforcement requests; they will send a marked-up pdf by EOD.

If you're good with 15 days and the TIA paragraph, we can proceed to DocuSign. We'll queue internal approvals and get back if counsel pushes different wording.

Best,
